name: Baseline
description: Endogenous fast-transition baseline: model defaults with 2025-level carbon prices and no further policy. Default-run figures (model state of November 2026; re-check with `npx tsx src/simulation.ts --scenario=baseline` after model changes): GDP growth ~3.8%/yr to 2050 and ~3.4%/yr over 2050-2100; electricity demand growth ~4.4%/yr over 2025-30 (IEA Electricity 2025 projects ~4%/yr to 2027); 2050 generation ~104k TWh (~1.9x IEA STEPS ~55k, faster because Way-et-al learning keeps solar+storage undercutting fossil); fossil share of electricity ~58% in 2025, ~14% in 2050, ~8% in 2075 and ~2% in 2100; warming ~2.1C in 2050 and ~3.1C in 2100 (AR6-consistent marginal TCRE). GDP 2100 ~$2,160T is above the SSP5 marker (~$1,240T; SSP2 ~$700T), 2017 PPP. NOTE: the GDP LEVEL is the model's weakest output. It is dominated by soft parameters, chiefly serviceEfficiencyGrowth and robotIntegrationExponent: a +/-40% sweep of the effective service-efficiency rate moves GDP 2100 from ~$1.2Q to ~$2.8Q (see docs/SENSITIVITY.md). Read the level as a band, the transition shape as robust. Not a replication of any IEA scenario.
